model_type: scenario-weighted owner-FCF DCF (component build, 10yr) with equity-impairment bear

inputs.net_debt_basis: ESTIMATED 31-Jul-2026 pro-forma: 472.1 (31-Jan-2026 reported, ex leases) - 283.1 (Abbott proceeds 1-Apr-2026) - 90.0 (seasonal WC unwind to FY-end norm) + 26.0 (H2 FY26 cash burn) = 125.0. Refresh at the FY2026 result (late Sept-2026).
inputs.total_debt_basis: 31-Jan-2026 loans and borrowings: RCF 273.0 + term loans 72.0 + NZD/CNH 29.4 + Bright Dairy shareholder loan 130.0 (all current; facilities matured 30-Jun-2026, shareholder loan 12-Jul-2026). Ex leases.
inputs.last_revenue_basis: TTM continuing operations to 31-Jan-2026 (ex North Island)
inputs.last_fcf_basis: TTM owner FCF to 31-Jan-2026 = reported FCF -32.8 - SBC 0.0 - interest income 0.56 - lease principal 6.16; includes the H1 FY2026 seasonal WC build and the North Island. Not used as the projection base (component build from revenue instead) -- see historical_growth.notes.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 Annual Report cash flow statement / statement of changes in equity: share-based payment (reversal) -NZ$0.536m FY2025, +NZ$0.399m FY2024; H1 FY2026 nil disclosed. Equity-award taxes nil (rights settled at nil consideration). SBC-zero market -- held at 0%.
inputs.share_count_basis: 603,198,098 ordinary shares on issue at 31-Jan-2026 (H1 FY2026 note 12), unchanged since the 1-Oct-2024 recapitalisation placement; PSRs immaterial and anti-dilutive. Held FLAT (no SBC to expense, no raise assumed in the flows).
inputs.balance_sheet_date: 2026-01-31 (H1 FY2026 interim, reviewed by KPMG with a material-uncertainty-related-to-going-concern paragraph); net debt adjusted for the 1-Apr-2026 North Island sale completion and estimated forward to 31-Jul-2026
notes: MODEL CHOICE: probability-weighted owner-FCF DCF (component build, 10-year horizon) with a DISTRESS bear, routed via .claude/skills/dcf-methods/SKILL.md. Synlait straddles two routing rows -- 'operating company, non-US/cyclical' and 'distressed' -- but is NOT in receivership, has forward cash flows, a NZ$307m asset sale just completed, and a 65% controlling shareholder that recapitalised it in 2024, so a pure asset/creditor waterfall would be wrong; equally a plain three-growth-scenario DCF would ignore the live going-concern qualification. The chosen hybrid keeps the house engine (so the dashboard reproduces every scenario) and puts the distress in the bear path and its 40% weight. Read owner-fcf.md in full including section 7.

REVENUE BASE: TTM continuing-operations revenue to 31-Jan-2026 = FY2025 continuing 1,590.2 (1,827.4 group less 237.3 North Island discontinued) + H1 FY2026 777.6 - H1 FY2025 779.0 = NZ$1,588.7m. The North Island (Pokeno + Auckland) business is EXCLUDED from every forward year because it was sold to Abbott on 1-Apr-2026; it contributed NZ$237m FY2025 revenue and a NZ$23.1m after-tax loss (NZ$8.8m in H1 FY2026), so its removal is earnings-accretive and revenue-dilutive. Y1 = FY2027 (year ending 31-Jul-2027). FY2026 (guided NZ$19-24m underlying loss, results due late Sept-2026) is treated as the FY0 stub and is NOT projected as profitable.

NET DEBT (company definition: bank debt + Bright Dairy shareholder loan - cash, EX lease liabilities): 31-Jan-2026 reported 504.4 - 32.3 = NZ$472.1m. Less NZ$283.1m Abbott completion proceeds received 1-Apr-2026 (of ~NZ$307m / US$178m gross; ~NZ$14m holdback and completion adjustments NOT credited) = NZ$189.0m pro-forma at 1-Apr-2026 -- but that date is the seasonal working-capital PEAK (net inventories+receivables-payables of NZ$129.9m at 31-Jan-2026 vs an FY-end average of ~NZ$37m over FY2022-FY2025: 0.9 / 52.2 / 96.7 / -1.9). House estimate of 31-Jul-2026 (FY26 year-end) net debt = 189.0 - 90.0 seasonal unwind + 26.0 H2 cash burn (H2 underlying result ~+NZ$4m per guidance midpoint, less one-offs, interest ~NZ$12m, capex ~NZ$14m, lease ~NZ$3m) = NZ$125.0m. This is an ESTIMATE and the single anchor most in need of refresh at the FY2026 result: see inputs.net_debt_sensitivity for the weighted IV at 189.0 and 85.0.

LEASE TREATMENT: (B) leases as operating cost. IFRS-16 lease principal (FY2025 NZ$6.0m, TTM NZ$6.2m, ~0.4% of revenue) is charged inside the flows as lease_cost_pct = 0.4 and DEDUCTED from historical owner FCF; lease liabilities (NZ$53.1m at 31-Jan-2026: 6.5 current + 46.6 non-current) are EXCLUDED from net_debt. Nothing is charged twice. The CSV TotalDebt column (557.6) INCLUDES leases; inputs.total_debt here (504.4) does not.

SBC: immaterial and SBC-zero in practice (FY2025 -NZ$0.5m on forfeitures, H1 FY2026 nil, historical max NZ$0.7m = 0.05% of revenue). Kept explicit at 0% in all scenarios; house and street bases coincide, band_position is null.
INTEREST INCOME: TTM NZ$0.56m stripped from owner FCF for consistency; the company is a net DEBTOR so the section-1 double-count concern does not arise and cash is netted inside net_debt.

SHARE COUNT: 603,198,098 ordinary shares (H1 FY2026 note 12; unchanged since the 1-Oct-2024 placement of 384.6m shares to Bright Dairy at NZ$0.60 and a2 Milk at NZ$0.43). Performance share rights are immaterial (<1m) and anti-dilutive given losses. Held FLAT in all scenarios; no equity raise is assumed in the flows -- the bear's rescue-raise arithmetic is a memo, not a projection. NOT 218.6m (pre-recap) and NOT 2.2bn.

TAX: NZ$330m gross NZ tax losses at 31-Jul-2025 plus FY2026 losses (~NZ$420m+ per the Analysis JSON); the DTA on losses was derecognised at H1 FY2026 (DTA 9.6m -> nil, DTL 1.9m). Cash tax modelled at 0% until cumulative EBIT approaches the pool, then ramped to the 28% statutory rate (base: 14% FY2033, 28% from FY2034; bull from FY2031; bear never). Shareholder-continuity (49%) is preserved by Bright's stable control.

CURRENCY: statements and flows in NZD (filings state NZ$'000); NZX quote in NZD. currency == quote_currency; no fx_note required. ASX secondary listing SM1 is a foreign-exempt compliance listing, not used.

PRICE: NZ$0.395 at the 2-Sep-2026 NZX regular close (Yahoo regularMarketTime 05:00:13Z = 17:00 NZST). Not after-hours. 52-week range 0.35-0.85; the stock fell to a five-month low on the 14-Aug-2026 profit warning.

TAKEOVER SPECULATION: media reports of a2 Milk / Fonterra take-private interest were DENIED by Synlait on 17-Aug-2026. No deal-completes / deal-breaks weighting is applied; the strategic-value angle is acknowledged in the bull narrative only.

DAIRYWORKS: retained (the 2024 sale process was abandoned) and is the group's only consistently profitable segment (FY2025 NPAT NZ$10.3m, ~NZ$23.5m EBITDA on NZ$324m revenue; H1 FY2026 EBITDA NZ$13.2m on NZ$220m). It is inside the consolidated flows, not valued separately.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: base-case steady-state revenue growth (Y5-Y10), NOT a historical CAGR
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR (+5.4%) is entirely raise-funded: NZ$200m (Nov-2020) and NZ$212m net (Oct-2024) of new equity against cumulative FY21-FY25 net losses of ~NZ$216m; organic equity CAGR is deeply negative. Revenue 5yr CAGR (+7.0%) is commodity-price-driven (milk price NZ$7.83 -> NZ$10.16/kgMS) and includes the North Island business sold 1-Apr-2026. EPS CAGRs are undefined (FY2025 loss). Owner-FCF 3yr CAGR is ~0% only because FY2022 and FY2025 were both working-capital-release peaks (+135.6m each); the 10-year median owner FCF is NEGATIVE (-27.4m). None of these series is a usable forward driver.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF = reported FCF - SBC - interest income - IFRS-16 lease principal (treatment B). SBC is immaterial (<0.05% of revenue, negative in FY2021/FY2025 on forfeitures) so the SBC-adjusted and reported CAGRs coincide. Historical FCF is dominated by capex cycles (FY2019 -320m capex for Pokeno/Dunsandel build) and working-capital swings (FY2025 +141.9m reported FCF was a release; H1 FY2026 -199.8m a build), which is why the forward model is a component build and not an FCF-CAGR extrapolation.

wacc_rationale: Single all-equity discount rate of 16.0% applied to unlevered owner FCF in ALL THREE scenarios (section 7(f), charge risk once; no per-scenario WACC). Built in NZD, matching the flows: NZ 10-year government bond ~4.5% risk-free + NZ equity risk premium 6.0% x beta 1.2 (cyclical commodity processor) = 11.7% base cost of equity. Structural premiums considered ADDITIVELY, each assigned to exactly one place so nothing is charged twice: (1) NZX micro-cap illiquidity / free float <15% (Bright Dairy 65.25% + a2 Milk 19.83%) -> +1.5pp in WACC; (2) controlling-shareholder / minority-governance risk (related-party shareholder loan, related-party China retail channel, minorities are price-takers on any recapitalisation) -> +1.0pp in WACC; (3) execution / leadership risk (CEO resigned May-2026 after 11 months, Chief Quality Officer gone, Acting CEO, no permanent appointment as at Sept-2026) -> +1.0pp in WACC; (4) refinancing / going-concern COST of capital (facilities and the Bright loan matured mid-2026; syndicate pricing and covenant waivers reflect elevated credit risk) -> +0.8pp in WACC; (5) going-concern PROBABILITY (KPMG material-uncertainty paragraph, H1 FY2026) -> 0pp in WACC; priced as the 40% bear weight and the equity-impaired bear path; (6) customer concentration (a2 Milk; top-3 customers 36% of HY26 revenue) -> 0pp in WACC; priced in the flows via the decaying Advanced Nutrition margin in every scenario and the a2-migration bear axis; (7) commodity / milk-price cyclicality -> 0pp in WACC; priced in the flows via mid-cycle (not peak) margin ceilings and the bear's thin Ingredients returns. Total: 11.7 + 1.5 + 1.0 + 1.0 + 0.8 = 16.0%. An all-equity rate is used rather than a levered WACC because the capital structure is unresolved (refinancing outcome unknown at build) and the tax shield is nil (NZ$420m+ tax losses). Reference points in this folder: MOV.NZ 16.5% (post-going-concern turnaround), AGL.NZ 19% (post-rescue-raise staffing), CDI.NZ 17%, 2CC.NZ 19%; a stable NZ mid-cap would sit at 10-11%. Debt cost cross-check: Bright loan interest NZ$10.2m on NZ$130m for ~10 months of FY2025 implies ~9.4% pre-tax; a 16% all-equity rate on flows that are 30-45% debt-financed is equivalent to a ~19% cost of equity, which is where a going-concern-qualified micro-cap belongs.
valuation_philosophy: SML.NZ is a going-concern-qualified, controlled (85% held by two strategic shareholders) NZ dairy processor 18 months into a second recovery attempt, trading at NZ$0.395 (market cap ~NZ$238m) against ~NZ$690m of book equity and ~NZ$1.59bn of continuing revenue. The standard owner-FCF DCF cannot be applied naively: (1) the historical FCF series is unusable -- the 10-year median owner FCF is NEGATIVE (-NZ$27m) and the two positive peaks (FY2022, FY2025, +NZ$136m each) were working-capital releases, so every scenario is a component build (revenue x margin path -> lease -> D&A -> cash tax -> capex -> WC) from the TTM continuing-operations revenue base, never an FCF extrapolation; (2) the balance sheet in the CSV (31-Jan-2026) predates the completed 1-Apr-2026 Abbott sale and sits at the seasonal working-capital peak, so net debt is a documented pro-forma estimate (NZ$125m) with a sensitivity showing the NZ$189m peak and NZ$85m trough alternatives; (3) the bear case is a genuine equity-impairment path, not a low multiple -- enterprise value fails to cover net debt and the equity is under water, resolved in practice by a controlling-shareholder recapitalisation; (4) scenario weights are 40/45/15 -- the bear is weighted at nearly the base case because the auditor's material-uncertainty paragraph is live, the refinancing outcome is unknown at build, FY2026 is a third consecutive underlying loss, and the CEO seat is empty; the bull is 15% because it needs Dairyworks, Foodservice, non-a2 nutrition AND a normal refinancing to all land. The result -- weighted IV NZ$0.22 vs NZ$0.395 -- says the market is paying for something the DCF does not: the option value of the controlling shareholder's strategic interest (Bright paid NZ$0.60 in Sept-2024, 50% above the then market) and consolidation speculation. That gap is the finding, not an error: a minority holder receives the DCF value only if Bright Dairy and a2 Milk let them, and the model does not assume they will. A negative or near-zero intrinsic value on the bear path is the honest outcome and has not been floored away; a floored-at-zero weighted IV is shown as a memo.

base.narrative: Base -- muddle-through, refinanced by the controlling shareholder. Bright Dairy rolls the NZ$130m shareholder loan and the syndicate refinances the halved (~NZ$200m) bank facilities on the strength of the Abbott proceeds; there is no further equity raise. The South-Island-only business (Dunsandel + Dairyworks) returns to a modest profit in FY2027 as the FY25-HY26 'manufacturing plan adjustment' one-offs (NZ$33m tactical raw-milk losses, NZ$43.5m manufacturing costs) wash out, but the structural picture is post-exclusivity: a2 Milk remains the anchor Advanced Nutrition customer at minimum volumes only, so the FY2018-FY2020 12-16% EBITDA margins do not return. Revenue dips 2% in FY2027 (Ingredients volume down, lower FY27 milk price) then grows 2-2.5%/yr on Dairyworks export growth, Foodservice UHT cream and incremental non-a2 nutrition customers; EBITDA margin ramps 3.5% -> 6.5% by FY2032 (FY2025 underlying 5.9%; FY2022 reported 6.8%) and holds. Capex 1.8% vs D&A 2.7% (maintenance on a NZ$600m PP&E base with no growth projects). Cash tax nil through FY2032 as the NZ$420m+ tax-loss pool is consumed, ramping to 28% by FY2034. Terminal growth 1.5%, cap 10x owner FCF; Gordon binds. Leadership: a permanent CEO is appointed and the Stabilise/Simplify horizons deliver, Scale does not.

bull.narrative: Bull -- the reset works and Synlait becomes a diversified, profitable South Island processor. Dairyworks keeps compounding (HY26 revenue +51%, GP +22%) on Australian, SE Asian and US private-label/branded wins plus the Bright Dairy China retail channel; Foodservice UHT cream doubles in FY2027 as management targets and stays profitable; Advanced Nutrition diversifies beyond a2 Milk (white-label supplements, Middle East ELN customer, Nutrabase base powder, Abbott base-powder access, a2's FDA US infant-formula approval adding a new line). Revenue grows 0/4/5/5/4/3.5% then ~2.5-3%; EBITDA margin ramps 4.5% -> 8.5% (still well below the FY2018-2020 a2-exclusivity peak of 12.8-15.8%, above the FY2022 6.8%). Capex 2.0% funds modest growth projects. Tax losses are consumed faster (cash tax 10% by FY2031, 28% from FY2033). Terminal growth 2.0%, cap 12x. Net debt is refinanced on normal terms and the going-concern qualification is lifted at FY2027. The bull case also captures the strategic-value angle behind the (denied) a2 Milk/Fonterra takeover speculation: a clean, SAMR-registered Dunsandel plant with secured Canterbury milk is worth more to a strategic owner than to minority holders of a distressed equity.

bear.narrative: Bear -- the going-concern path fails to stabilise and the equity is impaired. The a2 Milk Company shifts China-label and base-powder volumes to Mataura Valley Milk and its ex-Yashili Pokeno plant as minimum-volume obligations under the NPMSA step down, taking Advanced Nutrition -- historically the only high-margin product line -- with it; Ingredients stays a milk-absorption release valve with ~nil gross margin in a weak WMP market; Dairyworks and Foodservice grow but are too small (~31% and ~4% of revenue) to carry a NZ$600m single-site asset base. Revenue shrinks 8%/5%/3%/1% over FY27-FY30 and flat-lines near NZ$1.33bn; group EBITDA margin never exceeds 3.0% (vs FY2025 underlying 5.9%); D&A (2.8%) exceeds a starved 1.5% capex, so FCF is positive only because the plant is being run down. Cash tax is nil throughout (the NZ$420m+ of tax losses are never used). Terminal growth 0.5%, terminal cap 8x owner FCF. Enterprise value (~NZ$71m) does not cover the ~NZ$125m of pro-forma net debt: the equity is under water on this path, and the refinancing that the H1 FY2026 going-concern note depends on resolves by a Bright Dairy-led recapitalisation that leaves minorities with a small slice of a small equity (see rescue_raise_memo). This is the scenario KPMG's material-uncertainty paragraph describes.

entry_price.method: Price at which buying today, collecting the scenario's interim owner FCF and exiting in FY2036 earns a 15% IRR; terminal value REBUILT at the hurdle rate: min(Gordon@15%, cap x FCF_10), floored at zero. Probability-weighted across scenarios.
entry_price.note: Because the house discount rate (16.0%) EXCEEDS the 15% hurdle, each scenario's entry price sits slightly ABOVE its intrinsic value -- the same inversion as MOV.NZ. The 15% hurdle is not the binding constraint on this name; the going-concern outcome is. The bear entry price is negative: no positive price earns 15% on that path.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (min(Gordon@r, 10x FCF_10)). The 16% row equals valuation.base.intrinsic_value; the 15% row equals entry_price.base.entry_price. Today's NZ$0.395 sits between the 15% row (0.4035) and the 16% row (0.3575): the market price implies a ~15.2% IRR on the BASE path alone, i.e. the market is pricing the base case as near-certain and giving the 40%-weighted bear no weight.

sensitivity.note: Rows = WACC %, columns = terminal growth %; base-case intrinsic value per share (NZD). Terminal cap 10x owner FCF applies in every cell.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 40% (house default 15%): KPMG's material-uncertainty-related-to-going-concern paragraph is live on the latest reviewed accounts; all core facilities (30-Jun-2026) and the NZ$130m Bright Dairy loan (12-Jul-2026) have matured with Bright's support only 'preliminarily indicated' at the last filing and no refinancing announcement in the corpus; FY2026 is a third consecutive underlying loss (guided -NZ$19m to -24m on 14-Aug-2026); the CEO resigned after 11 months and the Chief Quality Officer has left; and a2 Milk is building alternative capacity. Base 45%: the Abbott sale did complete and did halve bank facilities, Dairyworks and Foodservice are growing and profitable, and the controlling shareholder has funded two rescues -- muddle-through is the modal outcome. Bull 15% (house default 35%): requires Dairyworks, Foodservice, non-a2 nutrition wins AND a normal-terms refinancing AND a stable leadership team to all land within the horizon.
probability_weighted.weighted_iv_equity_floored_note: Memo: same weights with the bear IV floored at zero (limited liability). House headline keeps the negative bear per folder convention (MOV.NZ, AGL.NZ, GEN.NZ) because the depth below zero is information about how far the enterprise value falls short of the debt.
probability_weighted.band_note: SBC-zero market: house and street bases coincide; the accounting-regime band collapses to a point.

bear_case_detail.equity_impairment: Bear enterprise value NZ$58.3m vs pro-forma net debt NZ$125.0m: equity value NZ$-66.7m, i.e. NZ$-0.111/share. The equity is under water on this path.

rescue_raise_memo.assumption: Bright Dairy-led recapitalisation of NZ$150m at NZ$0.20/share (750m new shares, +124% dilution), proceeds applied to debt
rescue_raise_memo.reading: (equity -66.7 + raise 150) / (603.2 + 750) shares = NZ$0.062. A raise at any price ABOVE the negative going-concern value per share transfers value from the subscriber to existing holders, so on this path a rescue raise is less bad for minorities than the unraised figure -- consistent with the Sept-2024 precedent, where Bright subscribed at NZ$0.60 against a NZ$0.40 market price (a2 Milk at NZ$0.43). The house bear therefore uses the HARSHER unraised figure. The genuinely worse outcome -- no rescue, creditors take the assets -- is 0 for minorities (limited liability), which is what the equity-floored memo captures.

bear_case_detail.what_would_move_the_bear_weight: DOWN: an announced, executed refinancing of the bank facilities and the Bright loan on multi-year terms; FY2026 result with the going-concern paragraph removed; a permanent CEO; FY2027 guidance to an underlying profit. UP: a rescue equity raise at a discount to market; further covenant waivers; a2 Milk giving notice on NPMSA minimum volumes; another manufacturing/quality incident at Dunsandel.

sanity_check.basis_note: P/E unusable (losses FY2021, FY2023-FY2026). Historical multiples are computed on a MARKET-CAP / EV basis (FY-end 31-Jul Yahoo close x shares on issue at that balance date) because per-share prices are NOT comparable across the Sept/Oct-2024 recapitalisation, which took the count from 218.6m to 603.2m at NZ$0.60/0.43 (Yahoo does not adjust for placements). The comparison window is FY2021-FY2025, the post-a2-exclusivity-peak era; FY2018-FY2020 (a2 exclusivity, 12.8-15.8% EBITDA margins, P/B 2-5x) is shown but excluded from the averages as a dead regime. EV/EBITDA uses underlying EBITDA where reported EBITDA was negative (FY2024) or dominated by one-offs (FY2025). Implied multiples are at the WEIGHTED IV with EV = equity + net debt 125 + lease liabilities 53.1 (like-for-like with the CSV TotalDebt basis). Mid-cycle continuing EBITDA taken as NZ$75m (FY2021-FY2025 reported median 44.2, underlying median ~68.8, both including the loss-making North Island now sold; base-case FY2029E EBITDA is NZ$97m).

historical_averages_ex_outliers.ev_ebitda_note: FY2021 (37.2x on NZ$32.6m trough EBITDA) excluded as an outlier; FY2024/FY2025 on underlying EBITDA

sanity_check.diagnosis: No trip. The check guards against a valuation that needs multiples ABOVE the stock's own history; here every implied multiple sits AT OR BELOW the post-2021 range. Implied P/B 0.19x vs FY2021-25 range 0.14-1.02x (min FY2024, the pre-recap distress trough); implied EV/Sales 0.19x vs range 0.42-0.89x; implied EV / mid-cycle EBITDA 4.1x vs range 7.2-15.3x. The current price itself is at a historical floor (P/B 0.34x, EV/Sales 0.26x, EV/mid-cycle EBITDA 5.6x), so an IV below the price is not a manufactured discount -- it is what a 16% discount rate and a 40% equity-impaired bear do to a 3.5-6.5% EBITDA-margin business carrying NZ$125m of net debt. The multiples the market DID pay (EV/Sales 0.4-0.9x, P/B 0.4-1.0x in FY2021-23) were for a group with a2-exclusivity and a growing North Island; both are gone. No fix applied; the gap to price is documented in valuation_philosophy as the controlling-shareholder / strategic-value premium the DCF deliberately does not credit.
